findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The embedded-post `.topic-meta-data h5 a` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch should keep 30% to preserve existing appearance; using 70% makes the author name much lighter/lower contrast on light themes, which is an unintended visual/accessibility regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix.

findings.title: Light-theme value for .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: Previously `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; now the light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` while the dark branch is 70% of $secondary. This darkens the hint text on light themes (and is inconsistent with desktop/modal.scss, which kept 70%/30%). Light-theme behavior should be unchanged.

findings.title: Group member .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now the 50%/50% pair, lightening the member name on light themes. Only the dark branch should have been added; keep 30% for the light value to avoid an unintended contrast change.

findings.title: Mobile group member .name light-theme lightness changed 30% -> 50%
findings.body: Same regression as desktop: the light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` moved from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%, lightening the text on light themes rather than only adding a dark-theme fallback.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed 20% -> 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`; the light branch is now 50%, noticeably lightening the heading on light mobile themes. Desktop kept 20%/80%, so mobile and desktop are now inconsistent too.
